_comment: Ratchet floor for tests/test_setup_blocks_agree.py. This number may only go UP.
It is how many leading commands (one per && link) every fenced setup block agrees
on -- measured, not chosen. Lowering it records an intended divergence and needs
the reason in the commit message; raising it locks in a new shared command.
Written by the scaffolder, because the count depends on which toolchains this
tree was generated with: a tree that also carries node shares one more command.
A number baked into the template would be true for one --language and red on
It varies by time as well, which the number cannot. Arriving through
bin/skeletor-upgrade into a tree scaffolded long ago brings the floor for a
fresh scaffold, not for that tree -- which may already agree on more. The
failure then reads UPWARD and names the depth to raise it to; that is the
ratchet asking you to lock in a gain, not a defect. Read the enrolled block
list in the message first: a rise can also mean a document left the
Read the test's docstring before changing either way.

Raised 3 -> 5 on 2026-09-06, and the enrolled set SHRANK in the same commit, which the failure message warns to check for. README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md left deliberately: both open by cloning and changing directory, which is the documented exclusion, because they address a reader who is not in the tree yet and needs the product's dependencies rather than the toolchain. Telling a user of `sb` to install pyright is wrong, and that is the divergence the exclusion exists for. What remains enrolled -- AGENTS.md and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md -- are the two contributor setups, and they now agree line for line.

Re-counted 5 -> 7 on 2026-10-15 with skeletor v0.57.0, which changed the unit from lines to commands. Same two blocks, same text: line one joins three commands with &&, so the five lines that agreed are seven commands. Nothing got tighter.
